sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日简报》。

sentences.en: As 2026 gets underway, so does a midterm election year for control of Congress.
sentences.zh: 随着2026年的到来，国会中期选举年也随之开启。

sentences.en: A campaign that will determine whether Democrats can operate as a check against the extraordinary power of President Trump
sentences.zh: 这场竞选将决定民主党人能否制衡特朗普总统的巨大权力，

sentences.en: or whether Republicans can hold on to every lever of influence in Washington.
sentences.zh: 或者共和党人能否守住华盛顿的每一个权力杠杆。

sentences.en: Today, my colleagues Annie Carney and Shane Goldmacher on the opportunities and perils for both parties.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事安妮·卡尼和肖恩·戈德马赫将探讨两党面临的机遇与风险。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月7日，星期三。

sentences.en: Annie, 2026 elections, here we come.
sentences.zh: 安妮，2026年大选，我们来了。

sentences.en: Here we come.
sentences.zh: 我们来了。

sentences.en: Or, I guess, here we are.
sentences.zh: 或者我应该说，我们已经在这儿了。

sentences.en: This episode is going to be kind of a roadmap and a primer for this year ahead in American politics because while a lot of eyes are on Venezuela right now,
sentences.zh: 这一集将作为今年美国政治的路线图和入门指南，因为虽然现在很多目光都聚焦在委内瑞拉，

sentences.en: in Congress, which you cover, the focus is on the reality that it is an election year.
sentences.zh: 但在你负责报道的国会，焦点在于这是一个选举年的现实。

sentences.en: A very big midterm election year coming up in November.
sentences.zh: 11月即将迎来非常重要的一场中期选举。

sentences.en: And November sounds very far away, but as you know well, in politics, that really isn't very much time at all.
sentences.zh: 11月听起来还很遥远，但正如你所知，在政治中，这其实根本没多少时间。

sentences.en: And there's just a ton at stake in this election.
sentences.zh: 而且这场选举事关重大。

sentences.en: So we are turning to you to talk about the Republican side of that election and how Republicans in Congress are now thinking about planning for
sentences.zh: 所以我们转向你，来谈谈共和党在这次选举中的情况，以及国会共和党人现在是如何考虑规划

sentences.en: or perhaps dreading this coming election.
sentences.zh: 或者说可能是在畏惧即将到来的这场选举。

sentences.en: I think that dreading is the correct word here.
sentences.zh: 我认为“畏惧”这个词用得很准确。

sentences.en: Republicans ended last year feeling very pessimistic about their chance of holding on to control of the House.
sentences.zh: 共和党人去年年底时对保住众议院控制权的前景感到非常悲观。

sentences.en: And that's in a really large part because their party has failed to fix what ails the American economy right now.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为他们的政党未能解决当前困扰美国经济的问题。

sentences.en: Namely, high prices.
sentences.zh: 也就是高物价。

sentences.en: High prices, high utility bills.
sentences.zh: 高物价，高额的公用事业账单。

sentences.en: Americans can look at their receipts and they are not doing well right now.
sentences.zh: 美国人看着自己的收据，现在的日子并不好过。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The receipts for the failure are literally the receipts.
sentences.zh: 失败的收据，字面意义上就是这些收据。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: And nothing better illustrates the dire situation the Republicans are walking into this election year
sentences.zh: 没有什么比共和党在选举年开局时所处的严峻形势更能说明问题了，

sentences.en: than the fact that Republicans set themselves up to start the year on an issue, health care, that has for years been their biggest weakness politically.
sentences.zh: 他们竟然选择以医疗保健这个多年来在政治上最大的弱点作为开年议题。

sentences.en: And just explain that.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下。

sentences.en: Why Republicans are going to be kicking off 2026 on health care?
sentences.zh: 为什么共和党人要在2026年以医疗保健议题开局？

sentences.en: Because in the final weeks of 2025, congressional Republicans were so despondent about their overall failure to confront affordability
sentences.zh: 因为在2025年的最后几周，国会共和党人对他们在应对负担能力问题上的全面失败感到如此沮丧，

sentences.en: that a handful of them actually break with their party leadership and join with Democrats to force a vote on extending subsidies to the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 以至于少数人竟然背离了党内领导层，与民主党人联手，强行推动了一项关于延长《平价医疗法案》补贴的投票。

sentences.en: So this vote is coming to the floor against Mike Johnson's wishes and highlighting an issue where voters, by and large,
sentences.zh: 所以这项投票是在违背迈克·约翰逊意愿的情况下提交表决的，它凸显了一个选民们普遍认为

sentences.en: think Democrats are much stronger when it comes to health care.
sentences.zh: 民主党人在医疗保健方面要强得多的议题。

sentences.en: And just as a political matter, what the Republicans did in the final weeks of December
sentences.zh: 从政治角度来看，共和党人在12月最后几周所做的事情

sentences.en: was enormous because they basically voted to endorse, in a real sense, the Affordable Care Act, which is public enemy number one for many congressional Republicans.
sentences.zh: 影响巨大，因为他们实际上是在某种程度上投票支持了《平价医疗法案》，而这对许多国会共和党人来说是头号公敌。

sentences.en: It has been for a decade.
sentences.zh: 十年来一直如此。

sentences.en: And you're suggesting that they're going to reinforce that approval for the ACA in the coming days.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是他们接下来几天还要加强对《平价医疗法案》的认可？

sentences.en: Republicans have been divided about what to do about the ACA for years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，共和党人在如何处理《平价医疗法案》的问题上一直存在分歧。

sentences.en: But this is how much swing district moderate Republicans are feeling the heat, that they feel like they needed to join Democrats and to fight for these extensions
sentences.zh: 但这也反映出摇摆选区的温和派共和党人感受到了多大的压力，以至于他们觉得必须加入民主党人的阵营去争取这些延期，

sentences.en: or risk losing their seats.
sentences.zh: 否则就有失去席位的风险。

sentences.en: And just because we're on the subject, will the Republicans breaking with their party
sentences.zh: 既然谈到了这个话题，共和党人背离党派的行为

sentences.en: help pass the extension of these Affordable Care Act subsidies in the House in the next couple days?
sentences.zh: 会有助于在未来几天内让众议院通过这些《平价医疗法案》补贴的延期吗？

sentences.en: It could pass in the House, but it doesn't seem that Republicans are going to pass it in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 它可能在众议院通过，但共和党人似乎不会让它在参议院通过。

sentences.en: And the president would never sign this into law.
sentences.zh: 而且总统绝不会签署将其变为法律。

sentences.en: He would not want to reward Democrats who have made this ACA extension the central message of their entire political strategy.
sentences.zh: 他不会想去奖励那些将《平价医疗法案》延期作为其整个政治战略核心信息的民主党人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we're going to begin this year, the next couple days, with Republicans having a big public battle among themselves,
sentences.zh: 所以我们今年开局的这几天，将看到共和党人内部爆发一场公开的大战，

sentences.en: one that's going to probably create a spectacle that reinforces the Democratic strategy that Republicans don't get it on affordability, especially the affordability of health care.
sentences.zh: 这场大战很可能会制造出一场闹剧，从而强化民主党的策略，即共和党人根本不懂负担能力问题，尤其是医疗保健的负担能力。

sentences.en: That's how Republicans are starting this election year.
sentences.zh: 这就是共和党人开启这个选举年的方式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I have to say that Tony Fabizio, Republican pollster who works for Trump,
sentences.zh: 我必须说，为特朗普工作的共和党民调专家托尼·法布里齐奥，

sentences.en: put out a memo last summer warning Republicans at all levels that if they did not get behind these ACA tax credits, it would be political malpractice and a disaster for the party.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天曾发布一份备忘录，警告各级共和党人，如果他们不支持这些《平价医疗法案》税收抵免，那将是政治上的失职，对该党来说将是一场灾难。

sentences.en: Now, some Republicans will say it's still early.
sentences.zh: 现在，一些共和党人会说时间还早。

sentences.en: There's a long way to go to November.
sentences.zh: 距离11月还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: They have plenty of time to change the conversation.
sentences.zh: 他们有充足的时间来改变话题。

sentences.en: But this is most definitely not how they wanted to start off this election year.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对不是他们想要开启这个选举年的方式。

sentences.en: Well, put this fight over health care into the larger, much larger context of dread that Republicans seem to be feeling right now heading into the midterms,
sentences.zh: 那么，将这场关于医疗保健的斗争置于共和党在进入中期选举时所感受到的那种更广泛、更巨大的畏惧背景下，

sentences.en: even if, as they say, they have plenty of time in theory to try to recover their footing.
sentences.zh: 即使正如他们所说，理论上他们还有充足的时间来尝试恢复阵脚。

sentences.en: So this is, you know, the latest chapter in a much bigger story about an incredibly frustrated, demoralized party right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一个关于一个目前极其沮丧、士气低落的政党的更大故事中的最新篇章。

sentences.en: All year, the White House has been driving this strategy of doing redistricting across the country, starting with Texas.
sentences.zh: 整整一年，白宫一直在推行一项在全国范围内进行选区重划的战略，从德克萨斯州开始。

sentences.en: And this was always viewed as something that you do if you are worried about winning the regular maps as they are drawn now.
sentences.zh: 这总是被视为一种如果你担心在现行选区地图下获胜时会采取的手段。

sentences.en: You would only bother to redistrict if you thought it would give you a political edge.
sentences.zh: 只有当你认为这能给你带来政治优势时，你才会费心去重划选区。

sentences.en: So the White House pushed this in states across the country where they thought they could gain a few seats.
sentences.zh: 所以白宫在全国各州推动了这一举措，认为他们可以在那里获得几个席位。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: By literally writing Democrats and their voters out of these congressional maps.
sentences.zh: 通过字面意义上将民主党人及其选民从这些国会选区地图中剔除。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But here is where a Democratic leadership that has widely disappointed voters for a long time really showed some backbone and pushed back.
sentences.zh: 但这就是长期以来让选民大失所望的民主党领导层真正展现出骨气并进行反击的地方。

sentences.en: Hakeem Jeffries, Democrat of New York and minority leader, was very aggressive in supporting tit for tat on redistricting.
sentences.zh: 纽约州民主党人、众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯在支持以牙还牙的选区重划方面非常积极。

sentences.en: If they're going to do Texas, we're going to do California.
sentences.zh: 如果他们要在德克萨斯州这么做，我们就要在加利福尼亚州这么做。

sentences.en: So it's basically set off an arms race that is adding up to pretty much a wash.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上引发了一场军备竞赛，结果几乎是相互抵消。

sentences.en: It's not clear that the redistricting battles across the country have given Republicans anywhere near the margin that they would need to feel confident about keeping the House.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚全国范围内的选区重划之争是否给了共和党人任何接近他们保住众议院所需的优势。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which means Republicans have to try to win the old-fashioned way, running on their record.
sentences.zh: 这意味着共和党人必须尝试用老派的方式获胜，即依靠他们的政绩竞选。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they don't have a lot to run on.
sentences.zh: 但他们没什么政绩可拿出来竞选。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: They've had full control in Washington for a year now.
sentences.zh: 他们在华盛顿已经完全掌控了一年了。

sentences.en: And they've really only passed one bill, the big, beautiful bill.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上只通过了一项法案，那个宏大而美好的法案。

sentences.en: Which is something.
sentences.zh: 那也算是一项成果。

sentences.en: It's something.
sentences.zh: 算是一项成果。

sentences.en: And they want to highlight the tax cuts.
sentences.zh: 他们想强调减税政策。

sentences.en: But that bill also included deep cuts to Medicaid that affect their voters.
sentences.zh: 但该法案也包括对影响他们选民的医疗补助计划的大幅削减。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it was an unproductive Congress.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个毫无作为的国会。

sentences.en: They've basically just said yes to everything that the White House wants.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上对白宫想要的一切都说了“是”。

sentences.en: Or just been totally cut out of the White House's decision-making process, whether it's shutting
sentences.zh: 或者完全被排除在白宫的决策过程之外，无论是关闭

sentences.en: down federal agencies or carrying out last week's military operation in Venezuela, which
sentences.zh: 联邦机构，还是执行上周在委内瑞拉的军事行动，这些

sentences.en: Congress was kept totally in the dark about.
sentences.zh: 国会都被完全蒙在鼓里。

sentences.en: They've given up their power, and they've just become miserable in the process.
sentences.zh: 他们放弃了自己的权力，在这个过程中变得痛苦不堪。

sentences.en: So the morale in the House is just terrible.
sentences.zh: 所以众议院的士气简直糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: When Marjorie Taylor Greene announced that she was resigning and leaving early, a lot of her colleagues kind of felt jealous, privately, they would tell me.
sentences.zh: 当玛乔丽·泰勒·格林宣布她要辞职并提前离开时，很多同事私下里告诉我，他们感到有点嫉妒。

sentences.en: Like, that sounds great.
sentences.zh: 觉得那听起来真不错。

sentences.en: It was how a lot of House Republicans felt when they heard that news.
sentences.zh: 这就是很多众议院共和党人在听到那个消息时的感受。

sentences.en: And are many of them thinking about or deciding to follow her out the door?
sentences.zh: 他们中很多人在考虑或决定追随她离开吗？

sentences.en: So what she did is, you know, announced that she's leaving early before the end of her term, which really doesn't happen unless you have a health issue or a huge scandal.
sentences.zh: 她所做的是宣布在任期结束前提前离开，这除非你有健康问题或巨大的丑闻，否则真的不会发生。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, you know, your voters elected you to serve out your term.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，你的选民选你是为了让你完成任期。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I don't think anyone else is going to follow her out early.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为不会有其他人会提前离开。

sentences.en: But a lot of people are choosing not to run again.
sentences.zh: 但很多人选择不再竞选连任。

sentences.en: Today, I am announcing I'm not running for re-election.
sentences.zh: 今天，我宣布我不再竞选连任。

sentences.en: One of the biggest examples this year would be Don Bacon.
sentences.zh: 今年最大的例子之一就是唐·培根。

sentences.en: So I feel emotional.
sentences.zh: 我感到很激动。

sentences.en: It's been a great 10 years.
sentences.zh: 这十年过得很棒。

sentences.en: He's kind of an old-fashioned Republican, a moderate from Nebraska, and he announced that he's going to retire.
sentences.zh: 他是一位老派的共和党人，来自内布拉斯加州的温和派，他宣布他将退休。

sentences.en: That's a huge blow to Republicans' chances of keeping the House.
sentences.zh: 这对共和党保住众议院的机会是一个巨大的打击。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because that seat will likely go to a Democrat in the next election.
sentences.zh: 因为那个席位在下次选举中很可能会落入民主党手中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it's not just moderates like Don Bacon who are leaving Congress.
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是像唐·培根这样的温和派在离开国会。

sentences.en: We've seen some lawmakers who call themselves ultra-MAGA head for the exits.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到一些自称“超级MAGA”的议员也走向了出口。

sentences.en: Elise Stefanik in the days before Christmas said she's going to retire at the end of her term.
sentences.zh: 埃莉斯·斯特凡尼克在圣诞节前几天表示，她将在任期结束时退休。

sentences.en: Having a member of the leadership team come out and suggest that the Speaker was a liar,
sentences.zh: 让领导团队的一名成员出来暗示议长是个骗子，

sentences.en: that he was a political novice, that he was all sorts of things that Elise Stefanik said is just unheard of.
sentences.zh: 说他是个政治新手，说他是个各种各样的人，埃莉斯·斯特凡尼克所说的这些简直闻所未闻。

sentences.en: She's been incredibly fed up with Speaker Johnson's leadership of the House, has been criticizing publicly and saying she's felt mistreated by him.
sentences.zh: 她对约翰逊议长在众议院的领导感到非常厌倦，一直在公开批评，并表示她觉得受到了他的虐待。

sentences.en: I don't exactly know why Elise won't just call me.
sentences.zh: 我不太明白为什么埃莉斯不直接给我打电话。

sentences.en: I texted her yesterday.
sentences.zh: 我昨天给她发了短信。

sentences.en: She's upset.
sentences.zh: 她很心烦。

sentences.en: Privately, she's been frustrated with Donald Trump and his treatment of her.
sentences.zh: 私下里，她一直对唐纳德·特朗普以及他对她的对待方式感到沮丧。

sentences.en: You have Nancy Mace.
sentences.zh: 还有南希·梅斯。

sentences.en: Republican Congresswoman Nancy Mace of South Carolina has an op-ed in the New York Times entitled, What's the Point of Congress?
sentences.zh: 南卡罗来纳州的共和党女众议员南希·梅斯在《纽约时报》上发表了一篇专栏文章，标题是《国会的意义何在？》。

sentences.en: Who has also been publicly critical of Mike Johnson.
sentences.zh: 她也一直公开批评迈克·约翰逊。

sentences.en: She writes in part, quote, Nancy Pelosi was a more effective House Speaker than any Republican this century.
sentences.zh: 她在文中写道，引用：“南希·佩洛西是本世纪比任何共和党人都更有效的众议院议长。”

sentences.en: She's not going to run for re-election, trying to run for governor of South Carolina instead.
sentences.zh: 她不打算竞选连任，而是试图竞选南卡罗来纳州州长。

sentences.en: So those two women really just speak to how demoralized a lot of Republicans, even those who have fashioned themselves after Trump, are feeling right now.
sentences.zh: 所以这两位女性真正说明了许多共和党人，即使是那些以特朗普为榜样的人，现在感到多么士气低落。

sentences.en: So with House Republicans being both unable to conquer the affordability issue
sentences.zh: 那么，随着众议院共和党人既无法攻克负担能力问题，

sentences.en: and becoming miserable in their jobs in the House, some of them retiring and making the seats very gettable for Democrats, others like Nancy Mace, Elise Stefanik, retiring,
sentences.zh: 又在众议院的工作中感到痛苦，一些人退休使席位变得非常容易被民主党夺取，另一些人如南希·梅斯、埃莉斯·斯特凡尼克也选择退休，

sentences.en: and I assume the seats will just be filled by other Republicans.
sentences.zh: 我假设这些席位会被其他共和党人填补。

sentences.en: What is the strategy for the Republicans in the midterms?
sentences.zh: 共和党在中期选举中的策略是什么？

sentences.en: What are they saying their message is going to be if they don't really like the message that's attached to them at the moment?
sentences.zh: 如果他们并不真正喜欢目前贴在他们身上的标签，他们说他们的信息会是什么？

sentences.en: Look, a lot of them think that affordability will be the strategy, and they have time to talk about it in a convincing way to their constituents,
sentences.zh: 听着，他们很多人认为负担能力将是他们的策略，他们有时间以一种令人信服的方式向选民谈论这个问题，

sentences.en: even if the president is calling it a hoax.
sentences.zh: 即使总统称其为骗局。

sentences.en: We'll see if that's going to work for them.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待这是否对他们有效。

sentences.en: Then, you know, I think for Republicans in competitive districts, the strategy is going to be saying, I stood up to my party.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，我认为对于竞争激烈的选区的共和党人来说，策略将是说，我反抗了我的政党。

sentences.en: I forced this vote on Affordable Care Act subsidies extension.
sentences.zh: 我强行推动了这次关于《平价医疗法案》补贴延期的投票。

sentences.en: That will be their case they're making, which will be a hard sell because at the end of the day, the subsidies will not pass.
sentences.zh: 这将是他们提出的理由，但这很难推销，因为归根结底，这些补贴是不会通过的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, what they did amounts to a little more than messaging, which can only take you really so far if the lives of your constituents
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们的所作所为充其量不过是传达信息，如果选民的生活

sentences.en: are still worse off while you were in office.
sentences.zh: 在你任期内依然没有改善，那么这种做法能起到的作用非常有限。

sentences.en: And then they're left with this hope that Democrats run people like Zora Mamdani, who are far left and progressive and socialist and convince their voters
sentences.zh: 然后他们只能寄希望于民主党能推举像佐拉·马姆达尼这样的人，他们属于极左、进步派和社会主义者，并说服选民

sentences.en: that that's the alternative, broadly speaking.
sentences.zh: 从广义上讲，这就是另一种选择。

sentences.en: And brand Democrats as radicals, even when in some districts, you know, they're absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 并将民主党人贴上激进分子的标签，即便在某些选区，你知道，他们根本不是那样。

sentences.en: So, what do you think the best case scenario for congressional Republicans, especially in the House, will be over the next 10 months or so?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为在接下来的10个月左右，国会共和党人（尤其是众议院）的最佳情况会是什么样？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not asking you to guess numerically what's going to happen in November's election, but in the Republicans' minds,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不是让你去预测11月选举的具体数字，但在共和党人看来，

sentences.en: how does this go really well and how does it go real, real bad?
sentences.zh: 怎样才算进展得非常顺利，又怎样才算进展得非常、非常糟糕？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I'd say that the best case is that they buck conventionalism and hold the House.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为最好的情况是他们打破常规，保住众议院。

sentences.en: They lose a few Senate seats but hold the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会失去几个参议院席位，但能保住参议院的控制权。

sentences.en: And I guess the worst case scenario, which I think is the one that more Republicans are really entertaining,
sentences.zh: 而我猜最坏的情况——我认为这也是更多共和党人真正担心的——

sentences.en: is this bad blood between Republican rank and file members and Speaker Mike Johnson could lead to, you know, ousting their own speaker before the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 是共和党普通议员与议长迈克·约翰逊之间的积怨，可能会导致他们在中期选举前罢免自己的议长。

sentences.en: That's a possibility.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可能性。

sentences.en: Could mean a loss of the House by a wider margin than anyone even thinks.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着失去众议院的幅度比任何人预想的都要大。

sentences.en: And then Democrats controlling all of the key committees in the final years of Trump's presidency, which would mean the Oversight Committee and the Judiciary Committee
sentences.zh: 然后民主党将在特朗普总统任期的最后几年控制所有关键委员会，这意味着监督委员会和司法委员会

sentences.en: potentially doing real investigations and demanding information from all of these agencies that are not sharing information with Congress, they would have subpoena power.
sentences.zh: 可能会进行真正的调查，并要求所有不与国会共享信息的机构提供信息，他们将拥有传唤权。

sentences.en: So it would change the dynamic in Washington dramatically for Democrats to regain control of the House.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果民主党重新夺回众议院控制权，华盛顿的动态将发生巨大变化。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Thus, the Republican dread.
sentences.zh: 这就是共和党的恐惧所在。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, Annie, thank you for that.
sentences.zh: 好的，安妮，谢谢你。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Happy New Year.
sentences.zh: 新年快乐。

sentences.en: Cheers.
sentences.zh: 干杯。

sentences.en: After the break, Shane Goldmacher on The Democrats.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，肖恩·戈德马赫将谈谈民主党。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“连接”游戏。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作“拼字蜜蜂”和“字母箱”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Jane.
sentences.zh: 简。

sentences.en: Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔。

sentences.en: Thank you for representing the Democratic side of the ledger in our conversation here.
sentences.zh: 感谢你在我们今天的对话中代表民主党一方。

sentences.en: If, as Annie Carney just told us,
sentences.zh: 如果正如安妮·卡尼刚才告诉我们的那样，

sentences.en: Republicans are filled with dread about their prospects, especially in the House in this year's upcoming midterm elections,
sentences.zh: 共和党人对他们的前景感到恐惧，特别是在今年即将到来的中期选举中的众议院席位，

sentences.en: doesn't that almost certainly mean that Democrats are filled with whatever the opposite of dread is?
sentences.zh: 那这是否几乎肯定意味着民主党人对恐惧的反面感到兴奋？

sentences.en: And what would that be?
sentences.zh: 那会是什么呢？

sentences.en: I would say that Democrats are broadly filled with an anxious optimism.
sentences.zh: 我会说民主党人普遍充满了焦虑的乐观情绪。

sentences.en: And the reasons to be optimistic are pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 乐观的理由非常明确。

sentences.en: They see over-performances in special elections, victories in November, and Trump's slipping approval ratings on the most important issues to voters, prices, and the economy.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了特别选举中的超常表现、11月的胜利，以及特朗普在选民最关心的议题——物价和经济——上的支持率下滑。

sentences.en: And they say,
sentences.zh: 他们说，

sentences.en: This is the kind of political environment that the Democrats were hoping for at the end of Donald Trump's first year.
sentences.zh: 这就是民主党人在唐纳德·特朗普第一年结束时所期待的政治环境。

sentences.en: One where he seems to be openly fumbling on the economy and mocking the idea of affordability.
sentences.zh: 一个他似乎在经济问题上公开笨拙，并嘲笑负担能力概念的环境。

sentences.en: Not just mocking it at times, but showing that he is focused on other things that are personal to himself, whether it is—
sentences.zh: 不仅有时嘲笑它，还表现出他专注于其他对他个人而言重要的事情，无论是——

sentences.en: Trump-Kennedy Center.
sentences.zh: 特朗普-肯尼迪中心。

sentences.en: Yeah, Trump-Kennedy Center, gilding parts of the Oval Office, building a ballroom while the government was shut down.
sentences.zh: 没错，特朗普-肯尼迪中心，装饰椭圆形办公室的部分区域，在政府停摆期间建造宴会厅。

sentences.en: That was his focus at the end of 2025.
sentences.zh: 这就是他2025年底的关注点。

sentences.en: And 2026 began with a focus on foreign affairs, on Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 而2026年开始时，他的关注点是外交事务，是委内瑞拉。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: With the arrest of Nicolas Maduro.
sentences.zh: 随着尼古拉斯·马杜罗的被捕。

sentences.en: And it doesn't exactly fit with the America First branding that he ran on.
sentences.zh: 这与他竞选时所宣扬的“美国优先”品牌并不完全吻合。

sentences.en: This is hardly a kitchen table issue for most Americans.
sentences.zh: 这对大多数美国人来说根本算不上什么切身利益问题。

sentences.en: And I think all of these things have fed into this image of a president who is focused on himself, on his reputation in history,
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些事情都加深了人们对这位总统的印象，他专注于自己，专注于他在历史上的名声，

sentences.en: rather than the personal finances of the Americans who voted to make him president.
sentences.zh: 而不是那些投票让他当选的美国人的个人财务状况。

sentences.en: And so I think that Democrats are starting to think that that image of a president who is distracted, who is self-indulgent, that that is starting to break through.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为民主党人开始觉得，那种心不在焉、自我放纵的总统形象，已经开始深入人心了。

sentences.en: And the trust that voters have had recently and historically in the Republican Party to fix the economy is waning.
sentences.zh: 选民最近以及历史上对共和党解决经济问题的信任正在减弱。

sentences.en: And plus, just historically, the party in power loses seats in the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 而且，从历史上看，执政党在中期选举中总是会失去席位。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the margins Republicans have are so small and so slim that even like a non-wave year should give Democrats a majority in the House.
sentences.zh: 共和党拥有的优势如此之小，如此微弱，以至于即使不是“浪潮年”，民主党也应该能在众议院获得多数席位。

sentences.en: And when you say margins, what you simply mean is, of course, that there are literally only a handful of Republicans in the Republican House majority.
sentences.zh: 当你提到优势时，你简单的意思当然是，共和党在众议院的多数席位实际上只有寥寥几个。

sentences.en: So even if they lose, what, three, four, five seats,
sentences.zh: 所以即使他们失去，比如，三个、四个、五个席位，

sentences.en: Democrats suddenly control the United States House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 民主党人就会突然控制美国众议院。

sentences.en: And so the environment is the reason for optimism right now for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种环境是目前民主党人感到乐观的原因。

sentences.en: But the anxiousness comes from some of the other factors, which is, well, what are those seats?
sentences.zh: 但焦虑来自于其他一些因素，那就是，嗯，那些席位是什么？

sentences.en: And what does the map actually look like?
sentences.zh: 地图实际上是什么样的？

sentences.en: And historically, there have been a ton of seats that have been up for grabs in the House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 历史上，众议院曾有大量席位可以争夺。

sentences.en: And that number is shrinking and shrinking.
sentences.zh: 而这个数字正在不断萎缩。

sentences.en: And it's really important because it means even if there is a, quote unquote, blue wave,
sentences.zh: 这非常重要，因为这意味着即使出现所谓的“蓝色浪潮”，

sentences.en: let's say Democrats overperform by seven or eight percentage points from what they did in 2024.
sentences.zh: 假设民主党的表现比2024年高出七到八个百分点。

sentences.en: Well, that doesn't capture as many Republican seats as it might have a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这并不能像十年前那样夺取那么多的共和党席位。

sentences.en: And if you take all the seats that are in the toss-up category and the leaning Democratic seats and you give them all to the Democrats, right, all the most competitive seats,
sentences.zh: 如果你把所有处于摇摆类别的席位和倾向民主党的席位都给民主党，对吧，所有竞争最激烈的席位，

sentences.en: they end up in like the low 220s.
sentences.zh: 他们最终也只有220出头的席位。

sentences.en: And you need 218 seats in the House for a majority.
sentences.zh: 而在众议院，你需要218个席位才能获得多数。

sentences.en: So even sweeping these toss-up seats just gets the Democrats over the line.
sentences.zh: 所以即使横扫这些摇摆席位，也只是让民主党勉强过线。

sentences.en: And is this reality that even a blue wave won't get Democrats that many seats?
sentences.zh: 这就是现实吗？即使是蓝色浪潮也不会让民主党获得那么多席位？

sentences.en: Is that just the extension of the conversation we've been having with you for years, the fact that there's been so much partisan gerrymandering,
sentences.zh: 这是否只是我们多年来与你进行的对话的延伸，即存在如此多的党派选区划分，

sentences.en: there just really aren't any purple seats left?
sentences.zh: 以至于真的没有紫色（摇摆）选区了？

sentences.en: It's partly partisan gerrymandering.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为党派选区划分。

sentences.en: It's also sort of a broader trend in America, which is self-sorting by voters.
sentences.zh: 这也是美国的一种更广泛的趋势，即选民的自我分类。

sentences.en: The blue areas are getting bluer and the red areas are getting redder.
sentences.zh: 蓝色区域变得更蓝，红色区域变得更红。

sentences.en: And so even if you're not intending to gerrymander people, they've self-selected into—
sentences.zh: 所以即使你无意进行选区划分，人们也已经自我选择了——

sentences.en: Right, we talked about this, the self-gerrymander.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们谈过这个，自我选区划分。

sentences.en: Yeah, into their own communities.
sentences.zh: 是的，进入他们自己的社区。

sentences.en: And so it's that combination that's led to a shrunken map that leaves less margin for error for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 正是这种结合导致了地图的萎缩，给民主党留下的犯错空间更小了。

sentences.en: What else beyond a map that makes it kind of hard for anybody to really pick up all that many seats will make Democrats anxious about 2026?
sentences.zh: 除了让任何人真的很难获得那么多席位的地图之外，还有什么会让民主党人对2026年感到焦虑？

sentences.en: The candidates, right?
sentences.zh: 候选人，对吧？

sentences.en: The Democratic Party has an unusually large number of intense primaries that they're facing next year because when you're tossed from power, you have some introspection.
sentences.zh: 民主党明年面临异常多的激烈初选，因为当你被赶下台时，你会进行一些反思。

sentences.en: What did you do?
sentences.zh: 你做了什么？

sentences.en: Where did you go wrong?
sentences.zh: 你在哪里出了错？

sentences.en: And who do you want to represent you in the future?
sentences.zh: 你希望谁在未来代表你？

sentences.en: And across the map, there are these primaries that are testing some of the disagreements that the Democratic Party has.
sentences.zh: 在整个地图上，这些初选正在考验民主党内部的一些分歧。

sentences.en: And so who emerges in those races is also going to be a pretty important factor.
sentences.zh: 所以谁能在这些竞选中脱颖而出，也将是一个非常重要的因素。

sentences.en: I mean, we said the Democrats have a pretty good chance to take the House.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们说过民主党有很好的机会夺取众议院。

sentences.en: It's really hard for them to take the Senate at the same time.
sentences.zh: 但他们同时夺取参议院真的很难。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Republicans have 53 seats in the Senate, and there just aren't very many opportunities for the Democrats to win the Senate in 2026.
sentences.zh: 共和党在参议院有53个席位，民主党在2026年赢得参议院的机会并不多。

sentences.en: There's Susan Collins, who is the only Republican senator in a state that Donald Trump lost in 2024.
sentences.zh: 有苏珊·柯林斯，她是唯一一位在唐纳德·特朗普2024年输掉的州里的共和党参议员。

sentences.en: You've got North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 还有北卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: It's an open seat.
sentences.zh: 这是一个空缺席位。

sentences.en: You've got Sherrod Brown, the former Democratic senator from Ohio, running again.
sentences.zh: 还有谢罗德·布朗，前俄亥俄州民主党参议员，再次参选。

sentences.en: But, like, even if they won all three of those states, Democrats are still not back in the majority.
sentences.zh: 但是，即使他们赢得了所有这三个州，民主党仍然无法回到多数地位。

sentences.en: That would only get them back to 50.
sentences.zh: 那只会让他们回到50席。

sentences.en: Right, and 50's not enough when the president is Republican because J.D.
sentences.zh: 没错，当总统是共和党人时，50席是不够的，因为J.D.

sentences.en: Vance would break the tie in favor of Republicans.
sentences.zh: 万斯会打破平局，支持共和党。

sentences.en: And Democrats have, by the way, their own vulnerable seats up too, right?
sentences.zh: 而且顺便说一句，民主党也有他们自己脆弱的席位要保住，对吧？

sentences.en: They have to win all those and hold their own seats.
sentences.zh: 他们必须赢得所有这些席位并保住自己的席位。

sentences.en: And there's real fear in House races and in Senate races that the party will end up nominating people who are either outside the mainstream, who have bad baggage,
sentences.zh: 在众议院和参议院竞选中，人们真正担心的是，该党最终会提名那些要么脱离主流，要么有严重负面包袱的人，

sentences.en: and end up costing them potentially winnable races.
sentences.zh: 最终导致他们输掉本来可以获胜的竞选。

sentences.en: Let's talk about some of these primaries.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈其中一些初选。

sentences.en: And what you're hinting at is a fight that both parties have been having for such a long time, which is,
sentences.zh: 你所暗示的是两党长期以来一直在进行的斗争，即，

sentences.en: is it healthier for a party to have primaries where candidates sort out which kind of Republican, which kind of Democrat they want to be in the general election?
sentences.zh: 对于一个政党来说，进行初选，让候选人理清他们想在大选中成为什么样的共和党人或民主党人，是否更健康？

sentences.en: Or is it just distracting and costly, and does it damage the candidate for the general election?
sentences.zh: 还是说这只会分散注意力、代价高昂，并损害候选人在大选中的表现？

sentences.en: It sounds like Democrats have kind of made that decision for themselves.
sentences.zh: 听起来民主党人已经为自己做出了决定。

sentences.en: You're saying there are a lot of primaries.
sentences.zh: 你是说有很多初选。

sentences.en: What are the main lines of conflict in these primaries in a place, for example, like Maine?
sentences.zh: 在这些初选中，例如在缅因州这样的地方，主要的冲突点是什么？

sentences.en: There's a number of lanes that the Democratic Party has disagreements over.
sentences.zh: 民主党在很多方面存在分歧。

sentences.en: The first is ideological.
sentences.zh: 首先是意识形态。

sentences.en: Are you a progressive?
sentences.zh: 你是进步派吗？

sentences.en: Are you a moderate?
sentences.zh: 你是温和派吗？

sentences.en: The second is a generational fight.
sentences.zh: 其次是代际斗争。

sentences.en: Are you from the old guard?
sentences.zh: 你是老一辈的吗？

sentences.en: Are you from the new guard or the next generation?
sentences.zh: 你是新一代的吗？

sentences.en: And one of the places that that is playing out is in Maine.
sentences.zh: 缅因州就是这种情况发生的地方之一。

sentences.en: You know, my father was a seventh generation Mainer who stood up for people who couldn't stand up for themselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的父亲是第七代缅因州人，他为那些无法为自己挺身而出的人挺身而出。

sentences.en: You've got the two-term Democratic governor who's seen as a moderate, Janet Mills, sort of the perfect vision of what a traditional top recruit is.
sentences.zh: 你有两任民主党州长，被视为温和派的珍妮特·米尔斯，她是传统顶级候选人的完美愿景。

sentences.en: Trump rips away health care from millions of Americans and drives up costs on everything from groceries to housing to trucks and cars.
sentences.zh: 特朗普从数百万美国人手中夺走了医疗保健，并推高了从杂货到住房，再到卡车和汽车的所有商品成本。

sentences.en: She's a proven winner.
sentences.zh: 她是一位久经考验的赢家。

sentences.en: She's the kind of person you would exactly want to run in that kind of place.
sentences.zh: 她正是那种你希望在那种地方参选的人。

sentences.en: This election will be a simple choice.
sentences.zh: 这次选举将是一个简单的选择。

sentences.en: Is Maine going to bow down or stand up?
sentences.zh: 缅因州是要屈服还是要站起来？

sentences.en: I know my answer.
sentences.zh: 我知道我的答案。

sentences.en: And yet she's facing a pretty stiff primary challenge from a guy named Graham Plattner who's gotten a lot of attention.
sentences.zh: 然而，她正面临来自一个名叫格雷厄姆·普拉特纳的人的相当严峻的初选挑战，他引起了很多关注。

sentences.en: When I tell people around here that I'm running for Senate, sometimes the initial reaction is, what the f***?
sentences.zh: 当我告诉周围的人我要竞选参议员时，最初的反应有时是，这他妈的是什么鬼？

sentences.en: An oyster farmer, a veteran.
sentences.zh: 一个牡蛎养殖户，一名退伍军人。

sentences.en: I did four infantry tours in the Marine Corps and the Army.
sentences.zh: 我在海军陆战队和陆军服役过四次步兵任务。

sentences.en: I'm not afraid to name an enemy.
sentences.zh: 我不怕指名道姓地指出敌人。

sentences.en: And the enemy is the oligarchy.
sentences.zh: 敌人就是寡头政治。

sentences.en: But also has gotten in a lot of controversy over a tattoo that he tattooed over that had Nazi symbolism, over a bunch of Reddit posts that he'd made in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 但他因为一个遮盖掉的带有纳粹符号的纹身，以及过去在Reddit上发布的一系列帖子而陷入了巨大的争议。

sentences.en: And there's a lot in the party say, so what?
sentences.zh: 党内很多人说，那又怎样？

sentences.en: He's unvarnished.
sentences.zh: 他直言不讳。

sentences.en: He's real.
sentences.zh: 他是真实的。

sentences.en: He looks like he solves all the problems that we've identified that the Democratic Party had in 2024.
sentences.zh: 他看起来像是解决了我们所确定的民主党在2024年存在的所有问题。

sentences.en: I truly do believe that we can build a system that is going to represent working people.
sentences.zh: 我真心相信，我们能够建立一个代表劳动人民的体制。

sentences.en: The number one response has been, well, thank God somebody's going to do it.
sentences.zh: 最主要的反应是，谢天谢地，终于有人要去做这件事了。

sentences.en: And guess who held one of the first big rallies for him?
sentences.zh: 你猜是谁为他举办了首场大型集会之一？

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders, who's playing in a number of these Senate primaries.
sentences.zh: 是伯尼·桑德斯，他正在参与多场参议院初选。

sentences.en: And so who emerges in these states is a real, real focus and concern for both sides of the party, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，这些州最终会涌现出什么样的人选，是党内双方真正关注和担忧的焦点，对吧？

sentences.en: There are people who point at Janet Mill and say, okay, sure, she looks like a great recruit.
sentences.zh: 有人指着珍妮特·米尔说，好吧，当然，她看起来是个很棒的候选人。

sentences.en: But guess what?
sentences.zh: 但你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: She would be the oldest freshman senator in American history.
sentences.zh: 她将成为美国历史上最年长的参议院新议员。

sentences.en: So right after Joe Biden, do you want to go back to that or do you want to take a risk at this really young, potentially inspiring guy,
sentences.zh: 所以在乔·拜登之后，你是想回到过去，还是想冒个险，选择这个非常年轻、可能令人振奋的家伙？

sentences.en: but who has said things that are easily clippable in Republican attack ads, self-describing themselves in ways that cast him as a radical.
sentences.zh: 但他曾说过一些很容易被共和党剪辑进攻击广告的话，他对自己的一些描述让他显得像个激进派。

sentences.en: And Republicans just love to use that kind of term, especially when candidates have used it in their own words.
sentences.zh: 共和党人非常喜欢使用这种词汇，尤其是当候选人自己也这么说过的时候。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is what Annie described as the kind of fantasy of Republicans that they can turn the entire 2026 Democratic slate of candidates into far left, out of the mainstream, Mom,
sentences.zh: 这就是安妮所描述的共和党人的幻想，他们认为可以将2026年民主党的所有候选人名单都贴上极左、脱离主流的标签，妈妈，

sentences.en: Donnie, Plattner, on and on.
sentences.zh: 唐尼、普拉特纳，等等等等。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: But we have no idea whether the reality is that these Democratic primary challengers might end up winning the primary and winning the general election.
sentences.zh: 但我们根本不知道，这些民主党初选挑战者最终是否真的能赢得初选并赢得大选。

sentences.en: I would think about it as there are two competing wings strategically in the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 我认为民主党内部在战略上存在两个相互竞争的派系。

sentences.en: Wing one wants to focus entirely on who on paper is the most electable candidate in 2026 because it is so urgent to take back power.
sentences.zh: 第一派希望完全专注于谁在纸面上是2026年最容易当选的候选人，因为夺回权力迫在眉睫。

sentences.en: And have a check against Trump.
sentences.zh: 并对特朗普形成制衡。

sentences.en: And have a check on Trump.
sentences.zh: 并对特朗普进行监督。

sentences.en: Let's do that.
sentences.zh: 我们就这么做吧。

sentences.en: Whoever in each state looks like they are likely as to win, do that.
sentences.zh: 在每个州，谁看起来最有可能获胜，就选谁。

sentences.en: And let's hold off on this conversation of populist versus progressive versus institutionaliSt.
sentences.zh: 让我们先搁置关于民粹主义者、进步派和建制派之间的争论。

sentences.en: Let's not have that fight in 2026.
sentences.zh: 我们不要在2026年进行那场争斗。

sentences.en: Reminder, not having that fight in 2024, pretty problematic.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，2024年没进行那场争斗，问题很大。

sentences.en: Ended up with Trump, right?
sentences.zh: 结果导致了特朗普当选，对吧？

sentences.en: And so they say that fight's going to happen in the presidential primary in 2020.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，那场争斗将在2020年的总统初选中发生。

sentences.en: Right now, we don't want that fight.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们不想进行那场争斗。

sentences.en: And there's a whole wing that says, actually, the primaries in 2026 are the appetizer to a main course in 2028.
sentences.zh: 还有整个一派认为，实际上，2026年的初选是2028年大选的前菜。

sentences.en: That have this fight.
sentences.zh: 让他们进行这场争斗吧。

sentences.en: These populist, these lefty candidates,
sentences.zh: 这些民粹主义者，这些左翼候选人，

sentences.en: we need to prove that we can win in the midterms in order to have a chance to sell the broader Democratic electorate that the left can win in 2028.
sentences.zh: 我们需要证明我们能在中期选举中获胜，以便有机会向更广泛的民主党选民证明，左翼可以在2028年获胜。

sentences.en: And so that's why all of these primaries for the Senate have become so interesting and so important and real proxy tests for the direction of the Democratic Party beyond the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么所有这些参议院初选变得如此有趣、如此重要，并成为衡量中期选举后民主党发展方向的真正代理测试。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So with all of this extremely useful context that justifies the term anxious optimism, I wonder if you can give us the best case scenario for Democrats in these midterm elections,
sentences.zh: 有了这些极其有用的背景信息来证明“焦虑的乐观主义”这个词，我想知道你能不能为我们提供民主党在中期选举中的最佳情景，

sentences.en: House and Senate, and then the worst case scenario for them.
sentences.zh: 包括众议院和参议院，以及对他们来说最糟糕的情景。

sentences.en: I mean, how much fun can we have with this?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们能玩得有多开心？

sentences.en: That's entirely up to you, Mr. Goldmacher.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于你，戈德马赫先生。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the best case scenario for Democrats is that Donald Trump continues remodeling bathrooms and focusing on things that voters don't care about,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为民主党的最佳情景是唐纳德·特朗普继续翻新浴室，专注于选民根本不在乎的事情，

sentences.en: that they beat Susan Collins, that they have a wave of these new recruits.
sentences.zh: 他们击败苏珊·柯林斯，他们迎来一波新的候选人浪潮。

sentences.en: They win dozens of seats in the House.
sentences.zh: 他们在众议院赢得几十个席位。

sentences.en: And they take power entirely in the Congress next fall.
sentences.zh: 并且在明年秋天完全掌握国会权力。

sentences.en: That's the best case.
sentences.zh: 那是最好的情况。

sentences.en: That's the best case scenario, politically.
sentences.zh: 从政治上讲，那是最佳情景。

sentences.en: Like, there is just so much that could go wrong for both parties still that the extremes of what is the best case scenario for Democrats and for Republicans,
sentences.zh: 就像，两党仍然有很多可能出错的地方，民主党和共和党的最佳情景的极端情况，

sentences.en: they're pretty extreme.
sentences.zh: 它们都相当极端。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, speaking of worst case scenarios, what is it for the Democrats?
sentences.zh: 那么，说到最坏的情况，对民主党来说是什么？

sentences.en: It's that Donald Trump starts focusing on the economy,
sentences.zh: 那就是唐纳德·特朗普开始关注经济，

sentences.en: that he sends checks to everybody in the country and he calls them Trump checks and they come in October just as everyone's casting ballots.
sentences.zh: 他给全国每个人寄支票，并称之为“特朗普支票”，而且它们在十月份发放，正好赶上每个人投票的时候。

sentences.en: He releases oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve and gas prices plummet.
sentences.zh: 他释放战略石油储备，汽油价格暴跌。

sentences.en: His new federal reserve chair cuts interest rates.
sentences.zh: 他任命的新美联储主席降低利率。

sentences.en: Everyone buys homes.
sentences.zh: 每个人都买房。

sentences.en: Things suddenly seem cheaper.
sentences.zh: 事情突然看起来变便宜了。

sentences.en: And people credit Donald Trump for fixing all of these things all at once.
sentences.zh: 人们把这一切归功于唐纳德·特朗普，认为他一次性解决了所有问题。

sentences.en: And Republicans don't just hold all those Senate seats we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 共和党不仅保住了我们谈论的所有参议院席位。

sentences.en: They flip Democratic seats and grow their Senate majority.
sentences.zh: 他们还翻转了民主党的席位，扩大了他们的参议院多数优势。

sentences.en: Democrats somehow come up short in the House despite all of the strategic benefits.
sentences.zh: 尽管有所有的战略优势，民主党在众议院还是以某种方式落败了。

sentences.en: And they have a four-year term for Donald Trump and complete Republican control in Congress.
sentences.zh: 然后唐纳德·特朗普获得了四年任期，共和党完全控制了国会。

sentences.en: I don't think either of those extremes are the likeliest outcome.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这两个极端情况是最可能的结果。

sentences.en: And I think that the Republican outcome is even less likely between those two.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在这两者之间，共和党那种结果的可能性甚至更小。

sentences.en: But there's a big range of possibilities for 2026.
sentences.zh: 但2026年有很大的可能性范围。

sentences.en: I'll say.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: Well, Shane, thank you very much and happy New Year to you.
sentences.zh: 好的，肖恩，非常感谢你，祝你新年快乐。

sentences.en: Happy New Year.
sentences.zh: 新年快乐。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, in a speech to congressional Republicans, President Trump beseeched them to try to keep
sentences.zh: 周二，在对国会共和党人的演讲中，特朗普总统恳求他们努力保持

sentences.en: control of Congress in this year's midterm elections in order to protect himself from a Democratic majority.
sentences.zh: 今年中期选举中对国会的控制权，以保护自己免受民主党多数派的影响。

sentences.en: You got to win the midterms because if we don't win the midterms, it's just going to be, I mean, they'll find a reason to impeach me.
sentences.zh: 你们必须赢得中期选举，因为如果我们不赢，那只会是，我是说，他们会找理由弹劾我。

sentences.en: I'll get impeached.
sentences.zh: 我会被弹劾的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, European officials expressed alarm over the Trump administration's suggestion made in the days since they ousted Nicolas Maduro that the United States could next take
sentences.zh: 周二，欧洲官员对特朗普政府在驱逐尼古拉斯·马杜罗后的几天里提出的建议表示震惊，即美国接下来可以接管

sentences.en: over Greenland.
sentences.zh: 格陵兰岛。

sentences.en: The real question is, by what right does Denmark assert control over Greenland?
sentences.zh: 真正的问题是，丹麦凭什么权利主张对格陵兰岛的控制权？

sentences.en: What is the basis of their territorial claim?
sentences.zh: 他们领土主张的基础是什么？

sentences.en: That suggestion was reinforced by Trump's top advisor, Stephen Miller, who told CNN, that as a matter of national security in its own hemisphere, the United States has a rightful
sentences.zh: 这一建议得到了特朗普高级顾问斯蒂芬·米勒的强化，他告诉美国有线电视新闻网，作为其自身半球的国家安全问题，美国对格陵兰岛拥有正当的

sentences.en: claim to Greenland.
sentences.zh: 主张。

sentences.en: For the United States to secure the Arctic region, to protect and defend NATO and NATO interests, obviously Greenland should be part of the United States.
sentences.zh: 为了让美国确保北极地区的安全，为了保护和捍卫北约及北约利益，显然格陵兰岛应该成为美国的一部分。

sentences.en: And so that's a conversation that we're going to have as a country.
sentences.zh: 所以，这将是我们作为一个国家要进行的对话。

sentences.en: In an unusual joint statement signed by leaders from Denmark, France, Germany, Britain, Italy,
sentences.zh: 在一份由丹麦、法国、德国、英国、意大利、

sentences.en: Spain, and Poland, European officials rejected Miller's logic and declared that Greenland's future should be determined only by Denmark and the people of Greenland.
sentences.zh: 西班牙和波兰领导人签署的罕见联合声明中，欧洲官员拒绝了米勒的逻辑，并宣称格陵兰岛的未来应该仅由丹麦和格陵兰人民决定。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Jessica Chung, Astha Chatharvedi, and Caitlin O'Keefe.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由杰西卡·钟、阿斯塔·查塔维迪和凯特琳·奥基夫制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Rachel Quester, contains music by Dan Powell and Alicia Buttu, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由瑞秋·奎斯特剪辑，包含丹·鲍威尔和艾丽西亚·布图的音乐，由克里斯·伍德进行工程处理。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格一起，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你获取播客的地方收听。
